Implementation Plan

**Implementation plan: issue "close-out-report" (project #7126, final step)**

Planning ref: `orchestrator/project-7126` @ `1cf4161509e3bd1465de8f7f096ebc6dc162db16`. The integration branch matches, so there is no mismatch.

Scope-mode: Hold Scope
Reuse-audit: extends analysis/recommendation-processing-report.md
Scope-mode justification: The issue names the exact edits: delete one source doc, add one ledger section, add one list entry and bump its count. Earlier close-outs already set the pattern. They used a per-doc `### \`analysis/<doc>.md\`` section with one bullet per finding and a verdict, then added the path to `## Processed source docs (N)`. No code, workflow, script or test changes. No new helpers, so Layers 1–3 of the reuse audit don't apply beyond extending the existing report. The full version costs the same as any shortcut, so there is nothing to boil.

**Automation / §20 surface**
- No new script, no changes to existing scripts or workflows, no scheduler wiring, no supervisor, no database work, and no entry in `docs/scripts-pending-removal.md`.
- The existing `apply-analysis` / `comprehensive-test-and-release.yml` path reads `analysis/recommendation-processing-report.md`. It keeps working: the processed-docs list grows by one entry in the same format.

**1. Files likely to change**
- Delete `analysis/workflow-optimization-2026-09-16.md` (563 lines).
- Edit `analysis/recommendation-processing-report.md` (1,110 lines; additions only).
- Leave alone: every other file under `analysis/`, including `last_collection_timestamp.txt`, `validation-selftest-status.json` and the other `workflow-optimization-*.md` docs. Don't open them.

**2. Edits**

a. Line 5: change `## Processed source docs (117)` to `## Processed source docs (118)`.

b. Add one line right after the last list entry (line 124, `` - `analysis/workflow-optimization-2026-08-29.md` ``) and before the blank line that precedes `## Downstream local issue ID recheck (repo-state only)`:
   `` - `analysis/workflow-optimization-2026-09-16.md` ``
   The list is in date order, so adding at the end keeps it sorted. Don't move any other line.

c. Add a new section at the very end of the file, after the last bullet of `## Conflicts / assumptions recorded for follow-up`, separated by one blank line:
```
### `analysis/workflow-optimization-2026-09-16.md`
Processed: <UTC date of the PR, from `date -u +%F`>
- <ID / short label> — <applied | already-implemented | rejected>: <one-line reason>
...
```
Use one bullet per recommendation, in this order:
- **Speed 1 / Cost 1 / Reliability 2** (`model_provider_broker_start` support-symbol preflight) — rejected (obsolete): the function no longer exists (only a historical comment in `scripts/implement_commit_changes.sh:122`). Review support is staged from the verified workflow commit, and the `REVIEW_EDITOR_PREFLIGHT` step exists (`review_autofix.yml`, `REVIEW_EDITOR_PREFLIGHT_ENABLED`).
- **Speed 2 / Reliability 1** (`resolver-agent-home` writability) — rejected (obsolete): the resolver runs in the review sandbox, and `resolver-agent-home` doesn't appear anywhere outside `analysis/`.
- **Speed 3** (reuse the AI-memory worktree across poll start/end) — rejected: the saving hasn't been measured on the current poller, and the change risks the independent fail-open memory paths.
- **Speed 4 / Cost 5** (lazy Semble in the poller) — already-implemented: `SEMBLE_BOOTSTRAP_MODE` defaults to `lazy` (`orchestrate_poll.yml:44`).
- **Speed 5** (no-action poll gate) — rejected: the sweeps and the merge-train release run every tick, and skipping them risks reconciliation.
- **Cost 2** (same-head deterministic failure suppression) — already-implemented: the `review-autofix-failure:v1` fingerprint cap.
- **Cost 3** (reviewer circuit breaker) — already-implemented: `REVIEWER_CIRCUIT_BREAKER_ENABLED`, `scripts/reviewer_failback_chains.json`, and the reviewer loop guards.
- **Cost 4** (prompt-growth reduction) — rejected: too broad to implement safely as written; `CONTEXT_BUDGET_WARN` telemetry already exists.
- **Reliability 3** (primary failure in run summaries) — already-implemented for the cited case: `conflict_resolver_failed` (`scripts/review_autofix_step_iteration_summary.sh`), `AUTOFIX_FAILURE_REASON`, and the failure headline.
- **Reliability 4** (memory fail-open aggregation / event_id) — rejected: under-specified; records already use stable IDs (`make_record_id`).
- **Reliability 5** (`ledger_emit_substate` warning storm) — already-implemented: `LEDGER_TOKENS_LOG_MAX_BYTES` tail read and `LEDGER_EMIT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`.
- **AI memory timing fields; GH_API_CALL / GH_API_SUMMARY telemetry** — rejected: broad cross-cutting telemetry; `GH_API_RETRY` logging exists.
- **Review gate double `/files` fetch** — already-implemented: there is a single paginated `/files` lookup.
- **Prompt cache 1** (aggregate `cache_hit_rate`) — already-implemented: `compute_cache_hit_rate` in `scripts/cost_audit.py`.
- **Prompt cache 2–4** — rejected: under-specified.
- **BUG-001** — applied: checks-gate-cancelled (`changelog.d/7127-checks-gate-cancelled.md`; `scripts/pr_checks_lib.sh` now treats cancelled, timed_out and similar conclusions as blocking).
- **CONSIST-001** — applied: checks-gate-cancelled. Gate D calls `_pr_checks_completed` with `N_BASE_REF`.
- **API-001, API-002 direct paths, DEAD-002** — applied: poller-api-dedup (`changelog.d/7268-poller-api-dedup.md`).
- **API-002 sweep-wide GraphQL batching** — rejected: the source tags it RISKY_SKIP.
- **API-003** (`gh_api_safe` in the release scripts) — rejected: the source tags it RISKY_SKIP, and it sits in the release retry loop.
- **API-004** — applied: guard-block-gh-retry (`changelog.d/7172-guard-block-gh-retry.md`).
- **BATCH-001, MERGE-002, REUSE-001** — rejected: the source's safety tags mark them RISKY_SKIP.
- **MERGE-001** — already-implemented: clarify comments are read once, paginated. Record this separately from the other RISKY_SKIP items, as the issue does.
- **MERGE-003 / MERGE-004** — rejected: batching would change the fail-open/fail-closed behaviour of the security-relevant lint scripts for a small saving.
- **DUP-001 … DUP-005** — rejected: style-only refactors that would add new staged support modules (risk of widening what gets staged).
- **EXPR-001 / EXPR-002** — applied in reduced form: implement-expr-limit (`changelog.d/7165-implement-run-expression-limit.md`). Expressions moved to `env:` and an 18,000-character guard was added in `tests/test_workflow_file_size_limit.py`. No scripts were extracted.
- **DEAD-001** — rejected: deliberately reserved (agents.md "Label-repair contradiction policy").
- **SHELL-001** — rejected: low value, and removing assigned identifiers conflicts with naming immutability.

Before writing "applied" for any item, the implementer re-checks it on the checkout. During planning I verified that all four sibling changelog fragments exist and the code they describe is present: the `pr_checks_lib.sh` cancellation comments, `N_BASE_REF` Gate D, the 18,000 guard in the size-limit test, and the guard-block `gh_retry` use. If one turns out to be missing at implementation time, record it as "rejected (deferred: sibling change not on this ref)".

**3. Data structures affected**
None. The only change is to the Markdown ledger; the count in the heading goes from 117 to 118.

**4. API / interface changes**
None. The report's format stays the same, and `scripts/apply_analysis_on_main` style consumers still parse `## Processed source docs` as before. `tests/test_apply_analysis_on_main.py` only writes its own fixture report.

## Decisions
### D1 — Where the new section goes
- Chosen: at the very end of the file, after `## Conflicts / assumptions recorded for follow-up`, because the issue says so literally.
- Alternatives considered: putting it with the other per-doc `###` ledgers (after the 2026-08-29 ledger, before `## Preserved machine-maintained artifacts`).
- Why: the issue explicitly says "Append a new section at the end … Append only; do not reflow existing content." Inserting it in the middle would contradict that.

### D2 — Recommendations the issue list doesn't name
- Chosen: map every source recommendation to one of the listed verdict groups. Narrative-only observations (Executive Summary, Orchestrator Health, Metrics Appendix, Per-Repo Breakdown) are metrics or evidence, not separate recommendations, so they get no bullets.
- Alternatives considered: one bullet per section heading, or inventing new verdicts.
- Why: §2 forbids inventing requirements, and earlier close-outs (e.g. 2026-08-29) also left out prioritization evidence that wasn't material.

### D3 — No changelog fragment
- Chosen: no `changelog.d/` fragment.
- Alternatives considered: adding a `changed` fragment.
- Why: this is internal analysis bookkeeping with no effect on operators or consumers. Earlier analysis close-outs didn't add fragments for the report itself.

## Security considerations
- Trust boundaries: none touched. Documentation only; no executable code, workflows or credentials.
- Authorization / new surfaces: none.
- External input: the source doc's text is untrusted. Its content is summarized in my own words, never pasted as instructions, and no command strings from it are run.
- Abuse cases: a PR body containing `Fixes/Closes/Resolves #7126` would auto-close the tracking issue (§21). Use `Refs #7126` and run `scripts/lint_pr_body_auto_close.py` on the body before creating the PR. Close the sub-issue with a keyword only if it isn't tracking-labelled.
- Money handling: not applicable.

**5. Risks and edge cases**
- Touching protected `analysis/` files by accident. Mitigation: `git diff --stat` must show exactly two paths, the edited report and the deleted 09-16 doc.
- A count mismatch between the heading (118) and the list. The listed entries and the stated count are only kept consisten
